The prose is unambiguous that Pantheon owns levels 1-6 and Swain owns two items, which is also what a 53.76% win rate over 731 games suggests, so the chart's Skill stages are conservative rather than wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns, and the level-6 spike attributed Swain's scaling to 'sustained AOE drain plus his root chains' without naming either ability.
audit.why: Death's Hand is 7s at rank 1 (750 range), Nevermove 12s (850), Vision of Empire 22s at 5500-7500 range, Demonic Ascension a flat 120s. Nevermove's 12 seconds is the window you actually trade in.
audit.corrected: Nevermove's 12s written into mid, Death's Hand's 7s and 750 range into early, Vision of Empire's 5500 into whys[4] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Land E pull into W root' — Swain's W is Vision of Empire and it does not root. The root is Nevermove, which the same entry correctly identifies as his E elsewhere. Separately, 'his W bomb' is treated throughout as a melee-range poke tool you face-block.
audit.why: Vision of Empire is a 5500-7500 range delayed zone that slows and reveals — it is a map-control and roam-catching tool, not the thing chunking you in a level-3 trade. His lane poke is Death's Hand (Q, 7s, 750), which the matchup never names once.
audit.corrected: Death's Hand named as the poke you face Aegis Assault at; Vision of Empire named for what it does — 5500 range, reveals, and it sees your Grand Starfall roams leaving; the phantom 'W root' removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ravenous Flock is never mentioned and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: Swain's passive heals him off every soul fragment he pulls, and Demonic Ascension is a drain. This is the matchup where anti-heal timing decides the extended fight, and the _missing-interactions file flags needs-antiheal for exactly this pairing. The page describes the healing problem in the late text without ever naming the fix.
audit.corrected: Ravenous Flock named in whys[6], spikes[3] and late; Grievous Wounds added as the itemisation answer in wants.you[1] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright'.
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will. There is no passive shield.

The only thing to fear is his E pull (Nevermove) — it's a slow-traveling skillshot, so sidestep it and his root never lands. Hold your E (Aegis Assault) to face-block his W bomb when he tries to chunk you, then W-Q in for the kill.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Burst him before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, 850 range — his only lockdown, and a dodgeable skillshot. Trade the moment it is spent. - Death's Hand: 7s at 750, his lane poke. - Vision of Empire: 22s, reveals your roam. - Demonic Ascension: 120s.

notes: The slot error here is 'Land E pull into W root'. Swain's W is Vision of Empire, which slows and reveals at 5500-7500 range; it does not root. Nevermove (E, 12s, 850) is the root, and the same entry names it correctly elsewhere, so the two got crossed. More useful than the naming fix: the matchup treated Vision of Empire as a melee-range 'W bomb' you face-block, when it is a map tool — the one that reveals your Grand Starfall roam leaving lane, which is a genuine reason to time roams around its 22-second cooldown. Swain's actual lane poke, Death's Hand (Q, 7s, 750), was never named anywhere. Finally, the late-game text describes drain healing beating your burst but never names Ravenous Flock and never mentions Grievous Wounds; the _missing-interactions file flags needs-antiheal for this pairing and it is now written into the itemisation advice.
